hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-owned, self-describing settings contract feeds a native JetBrains Settings page that renders whatever the daemon reports. The plugin adds config gateway methods behind the established sealed three-state result pattern and a native applicationConfigurable built purely from the daemon's description. Reads use the catalog IPC plus the existing value read; writes reuse the existing segment-aware write. The plugin owns no settings semantics; the daemon stays the single source of truth.

ownedContracts.name: Settings write surface (segment-aware write + clear) behind a sealed SaveResult
ownedContracts.purpose: The one way the IDE persists an edit: a plugin gateway write that maps an edited key to config.write's literal segment array and a clear that removes a key, each returning a sealed result distinguishing a persisted save from a daemon rejection or unavailability. Satisfies k4; first needed at s3, reused by both override editors.

consumedContracts.name: Self-describing settings catalog (enriched ConfigOption + role taxonomy) over config.catalog, and its plugin read surface
consumedContracts.purpose: The single daemon-owned description the whole IDE surface renders from, delivered over one read IPC and mirrored as plugin DTOs behind a sealed read result.

consumedContracts.name: Settings page framework (Configurable host + grouped collapsible rendering + type→control mapping)
consumedContracts.purpose: The native applicationConfigurable and its rendering scaffold: collapsible group panels, type→control mapping, default/current display, and the extension points where editing and dynamic-key sub-sections plug in.

boundary.internal: Private to s3: the per-type edit controls (chooser/toggle/number/text), field-level validation before save, dirty tracking against the last-saved value, the reset-to-default affordance, and the write-rejected surfacing that preserves the pending edit. s3 exposes only the write surface (sc2) for the override editors to reuse.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Daemon-side catalog enrichment + config.catalog assembly + contract-test/reconcile extensions stay private to s1; other stories consume only the payload shape (sc1).
Read-only rendering, collapsible layout + expand/collapse state, and the daemon-unavailable placeholder stay private to s2; the edit-capable row variant and dirty/apply logic are s3's.
The per-role overrides sub-section (models.tasks.<roleId>) is wholly private to s4; it plugs into sc3's section seam and reuses sc2.
The per-repo overrides sub-section (models.byRepo.<repoPath>.*) is wholly private to s5; it plugs into sc3's section seam and reuses sc2.

nonFunctional.performance: One config.catalog round-trip on open plus the existing value read; rendering + editing 31 settings is trivial Swing work. No polling; the page reads on open and after Apply.
nonFunctional.security: No new surface beyond the existing local Unix-socket transport; secrets/keys stay out of scope. Writes go only to the daemon's existing config.json via config.write.
nonFunctional.observability: config.write already logs each write; the plugin surfaces daemon-unavailable and write-rejected states rather than failing silently.
nonFunctional.durability: Persistence unchanged — the daemon's config.json write + reconcile own durability; the plugin never writes config.json directly.

api.name: DaemonGateway.writeSetting
api.signature: fun writeSetting(pathSegments: List<String>, value: Any?): SaveResult

parameters.name: pathSegments
parameters.purpose: The config key as LITERAL segments (never a dotted string), passed verbatim as config.write's path array so a dotted dynamic key is never mis-nested (lc1/k4).

parameters.name: value
parameters.purpose: The already-parsed, type-correct value (Boolean/number/String) so the daemon stores the right JSON type; never the raw editor string.

returns.meaning: Saved on config.write ok=true; Rejected(reason) on ok=false; Unavailable(reason) on socket down / result.error / RuntimeException.

errors.condition: config.write reply ok=false (invalid path / empty segment refused).
DaemonUnavailableException, transport result.error, or a RuntimeException.

preconditions: value already parsed + validated by SettingsEditModel.
postconditions: On Saved the daemon wrote config.json and ran reloadChatConfig (ac2).
Never throws — every failure is a sealed SaveResult (ac4).

api.name: DaemonGateway.clearSetting

parameters.name: pathSegments
parameters.purpose: The config key to REMOVE, as literal segments. Reset-to-default of a global setting (s3) and override removal (s4/s5).

returns.meaning: Same three-state classification; Saved means the key was removed and the daemon default now applies.

postconditions: Implemented as config.write with the value field OMITTED → JSON.stringify drops the undefined leaf → key removed; daemon config.write reused UNCHANGED (k3/k4).
After a Saved clear the setting reads isSet=false and renders the daemon default (ac3).

api.name: SettingsEditModel
api.signature: class SettingsEditModel(catalog: SettingsCatalogDto) { fun editField(path: String, rawInput: Any?): Unit; fun revertField(path: String): Unit; fun markResetToDefault(path: String): Unit; fun isModified(): Boolean; fun validationError(path: String): String?; fun collectDirty(): List<PendingWrite>; fun onSaved(path: String): Unit }

parameters.name: catalog
parameters.purpose: The daemon self-description (sc1) the model builds one FieldState per option from; default/type/enumValues drive control choice + validation, currentValue/isSet seed the last-saved value.

returns.meaning: Pure headless edit state: per-field pending value, dirty-vs-last-saved, per-type validation, and segment/op mapping. Load-bearing logic lives here (not in the Swing shell) so it is unit-testable.

errors.condition: edit/revert/markResetToDefault called with a path not in the catalog (programmer error).

preconditions: editField rawInput mapped from the control (Boolean/String) but not yet type-parsed — the model parses+validates.
postconditions: isModified() true iff any field's pending differs from last-saved OR is reset-to-default while set.
collectDirty() returns only changed fields as PendingWrite(segments, Set(parsed)|Clear); a validationError field is excluded.
onSaved(path) advances last-saved (or clears it for a reset) and clears dirty.
A parsed value equal to last-saved is NOT dirty — unchanged settings never written (ac2).

api.name: InsrcSettingsConfigurable.apply
api.signature: override fun apply(): Unit  // + isModified(): Boolean, reset(): Unit

returns.meaning: Native Apply backed by SettingsEditModel: per PendingWrite calls writeSetting/clearSetting, advances via onSaved on Saved; Rejected/Unavailable preserve the edit and surface the failure (ac4). isModified() delegates to the model; reset() reverts all fields to last-saved (ac3).

errors.condition: A field fails validation, or a write returns not-Saved — apply throws so the Settings dialog blocks and shows the message, preserving the edit (ac4).

preconditions: The page rendered from a Loaded SettingsCatalogResult (an Unavailable page installs no editors — unchanged from S002).
postconditions: Only dirty keys written; unchanged keys untouched (ac2).
A partial failure advances the Saved ones and leaves the failed one dirty with its edit + a surfaced message (ac4).

dataModelChanges.details: New sealed interface in the daemon package beside SettingsCatalogResult: Saved (data object), Rejected(reason: String), Unavailable(reason: String). The sc2 three-state result.

New pure data types in the settings package: PendingWrite(segments: List<String>, op: WriteOp) and WriteOp { Set(value: Any?) | Clear }. collectDirty() emits these; the Configurable maps Set→writeSetting and Clear→clearSetting. Keeps segment/op selection in the testable layer.

Per-option pure state: the ConfigOptionDto, the last-saved value (currentValue when isSet else an unset sentinel), the pending edited value, a resetToDefault flag, and a derived validationError. Number parsing tolerates the Gson-Double catalog shape (S002 numeric lesson) so an integral last-saved value compares equal to an integral edit. Private to s3.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: s3 OWNS sc2: adds writeSetting/clearSetting + the sealed SaveResult to DaemonGateway (+ DaemonGatewayImpl over rpc.call(METHOD_CONFIG_WRITE) + the DaemonGatewayService delegate + the 4 test doubles). writeSetting sends config.write({path: segments, value}); clearSetting sends config.write({path: segments}) with value omitted. Both exercised in-story so s4/s5 inherit a tested surface.

Consumes settingsCatalog(): SettingsCatalogResult UNCHANGED; the edit model reads each ConfigOptionDto's type/default/enumValues/currentValue/isSet to choose the control, seed last-saved, and validate. Forks no schema, adds no field.

Consumes the s2 Configurable scaffold: replaces readOnlyControl with edit-capable controls and wires the native isModified/apply/reset (S002 no-ops) to SettingsEditModel; groupsOf + collapsible layout unchanged. Registers NO SettingsSection (that seam is for s4/s5).

errorCases.scenario: The daemon rejects a write (config.write returns ok=false).
errorCases.detection: DaemonGatewayImpl sees DaemonResult.ok==false with no thrown exception → SaveResult.Rejected(reason) (generic reason when the bare {ok:false} carries no error string).
errorCases.response: apply does not advance last-saved, keeps the field dirty with the edit intact, throws ConfigurationException naming the setting so the dialog stays open.
errorCases.userImpact: Clear failure message; pending edit preserved; never a false success (ac4).

errorCases.scenario: The daemon is down / socket unreachable at apply.
errorCases.detection: rpc.call throws DaemonUnavailableException (or transport surfaces result.error) → SaveResult.Unavailable(reason).
errorCases.response: Same preserve-and-surface as Rejected but the message says 'unavailable'; already-Saved fields stay saved.
errorCases.userImpact: Told the daemon is unavailable, can retry; no edit lost (ac4).

errorCases.scenario: Partial-batch failure: several dirty fields, one not Saved mid-loop.
errorCases.detection: apply records per-field SaveResult and detects at least one non-Saved.
errorCases.response: Saved fields advanced via onSaved; failed field(s) stay dirty with edits; apply throws ConfigurationException summarizing failures; no rollback of the already-persisted Saved writes.
errorCases.userImpact: Honest partial progress; failures' edits preserved (ac2/ac4).

errorCases.scenario: A field fails type validation before any write.
errorCases.detection: SettingsEditModel.validationError(path) non-null; collectDirty excludes it and apply checks for any validationError first.
errorCases.response: apply throws ConfigurationException pointing at the field BEFORE any config.write, so nothing invalid reaches the daemon.
errorCases.userImpact: Guided to fix; nothing invalid persisted (ac1/ac4).

edgeCases.input: A number setting whose default/currentValue arrived as Gson Double 40.0 and the developer re-types '40'.
edgeCases.expected: Parsed and compared numerically to 40.0 as EQUAL → not dirty → no write (S002 integral-Double lesson). Editing to '41' is dirty and writes the JVM number 41.

edgeCases.input: Reset-to-default on a setting that is currently unset.
edgeCases.expected: No-op: markResetToDefault leaves it not-dirty (no key to remove); apply issues no clearSetting (ac2/ac3).

edgeCases.input: Reset-to-default on a setting set to a non-default value, then Apply.
edgeCases.expected: PendingWrite(segments, Clear) → clearSetting → config.write value omitted → key removed → next catalog shows isSet=false rendering the default (ac3).
Every pending value returns to last-saved, resetToDefault flags clear, isModified()=false, no daemon call (ac3).

edgeCases.input: The page opened while the daemon was Unavailable, then Apply invoked.
edgeCases.expected: No editors installed (S002 placeholder) → no dirty state → apply is a no-op.

edgeCases.input: A string setting edited to an empty string.
edgeCases.expected: Empty string is a VALID string, written verbatim as "" via writeSetting (distinct from clearSetting which omits value).

invariantsToPreserve.text: A setting write goes through the daemon's segment-aware config.write with a LITERAL segment array (never a naive dotted split); s3 passes segments verbatim and adds no daemon-side write logic.

The plugin talks to the daemon only over the existing Unix-socket JSON-RPC transport and honours its ok/error framing (ok=false→Rejected, thrown/result.error→Unavailable); no new transport, no direct config.json write.
The daemon stays the single source of truth for schema/defaults/reconcile; the plugin persists no default of its own — reset-to-default REMOVES the key so the daemon default governs.
The recognized-settings catalog stays the single definition site the surface renders from; s3 forks no schema and adds no field to the catalog or DTO.

testLevels.purpose: Prove the load-bearing edit logic headlessly (the review-epic split): type→control, per-type parse/validate, dirty-vs-last-saved, reset semantics, segment/op mapping.
subjects: number parse + integral-Double equality, enum-membership, empty-string-valid
isModified/collectDirty emits only changed fields; validationError excluded
fixturesNeeded: An in-memory SettingsCatalogDto with one option of each type, some set some unset

testLevels.purpose: Prove sc2 gateway classification against the real transport framing (extends SettingsCatalogGatewayTest).
subjects: clearSetting OMITS the value key; ok=true→Saved
fixturesNeeded: WireRpc replaying a canned reply through parse

testLevels.purpose: Guard the Swing shell wiring by source-scan (not headlessly bootable), extending InsrcSettingsConfigurableTest.
subjects: apply calls gateway.writeSetting/clearSetting (not a raw config.write string), delegates isModified/reset to the model, throws ConfigurationException on not-Saved/validation
edit-capable controls installed per type (not the S002 read-only JLabel/disabled checkbox)

provingTests: InsrcSettingsConfigurable source-scan: edit-capable controls per type
writeSetting sends {path: segments, value} and ok=true→Saved
integral-Double equality: re-typing the same number is not dirty
not-Saved apply keeps the field dirty (onSaved not called); validationError excludes + surfaces
source-scan: apply throws ConfigurationException on not-Saved/validation

testStrategy.testFramework: JUnit5 (org.junit.jupiter) on JDK21 via ./gradlew test, matching S002's SettingsViewTest/SettingsCatalogGatewayTest; source-scan tests read the Kotlin source. No BasePlatformTestCase and no daemon/TS test (config.write unchanged, already covered by src/config write-path tests).

migration.stateBefore: After S002 (main d6552ef) the Settings page is READ-ONLY: readOnlyControl renders a disabled checkbox/label and isModified/apply/reset are no-ops; DaemonGateway has settingsCatalog() but no write. The daemon's config.write + segment-aware write-path exist and are tested but nothing in the plugin calls them.
migration.stateAfter: The page is EDITABLE for global settings: type-appropriate controls, a pure SettingsEditModel for validation + dirty + reset, native isModified/apply/reset backed by it, Apply writing only dirty keys through sc2 (writeSetting/clearSetting) with preserve-on-failure, and a reset-to-default that clears the key. The daemon is UNCHANGED; per-role/per-repo sub-sections remain unbuilt (s4/s5).

migrationSteps.action: Add the sc2 surface: sealed SaveResult + writeSetting/clearSetting on DaemonGateway + DaemonGatewayImpl (clearSetting omits value) + the DaemonGatewayService delegate + stubs in the 4 test doubles. Additive to the interface.
Add the pure SettingsEditModel + PendingWrite/WriteOp/FieldState with per-type parse/validate, dirty tracking, reset semantics, and path→segments mapping. No existing symbol changes.

Replace readOnlyControl with edit-capable controls bound to the model and wire isModified/apply/reset (apply calls sc2 per dirty PendingWrite, throws ConfigurationException on not-Saved/validation). Unavailable placeholder + layout untouched.
Extend the test suite (SettingsEditModel, gateway classification + WireRpc, Configurable source-scan) and run ./gradlew test on JDK21.

migration.backwardCompat: The DaemonGateway interface only GAINS methods; settingsCatalog() and all S001/S002 behaviour are unchanged. The daemon's config.write is reused verbatim (no daemon code change), so config.json stays valid and older/newer daemons interoperate. reset-to-default is a key removal via config.write-with-value-omitted (existing unchanged daemon behaviour) — no new IPC or migration. A page against an Unavailable daemon falls back to the S002 read-only placeholder. Values already on disk render exactly as before; editing writes only changed keys.

alternativesConsidered.name: Pure edit-model + three-state SaveResult; reset-to-default = clear the key
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A headless SettingsEditModel owns per-option editor state/validation/dirty/segment-mapping; sc2 = writeSetting/clearSetting returning Saved|Rejected|Unavailable; reset-to-default is a clearSetting (config.write with value omitted).
alternativesConsidered.approach: A pure headless model holds one FieldState per option (last-saved, pending, per-type parse+validate, isDirty, segment mapping); apply() collects only dirty fields and calls writeSetting or, for a reset, clearSetting, advancing last-saved on Saved and preserving the edit on Rejected/Unavailable. The Swing Configurable is a thin shell delegating isModified/apply/reset to the model.
pros: Load-bearing logic is headlessly unit-testable (review-epic split).
reset-to-default=clear keeps k4 exact and truly returns the setting to the daemon default (isSet→false).
No daemon change (config.write reused for write + clear).
Three-state SaveResult separates rejection from unavailability (ac4).
cons: The clear-via-value-omission relies on config.write treating an absent value as undefined — must be pinned by a gateway test.

alternativesConsidered.name: In-shell edit logic (no pure model); controls self-track dirty
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep all edit/validate/dirty logic inside the Swing shell; controls capture a baseline and apply() walks components; sc2 SaveResult identical.
alternativesConsidered.approach: No separate model; each control captures its baseline, isModified walks components, apply parses/validates inline and calls writeSetting per dirty control.
cons: Load-bearing validation/dirty/segment logic lives in the untestable Swing shell — the silent-defect gap the review epic keeps catching.
Per-type parse/validate scattered; harder for s4/s5 to reuse.
Walking live Swing components for dirty state is fragile and EDT-coupled.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Puts validation/dirty/preserve-on-failure in the untestable shell — partial on ac2/ac3/ac4, exactly the class of silent UI defect the review split exists to prevent.

alternativesConsidered.name: Pure model, but reset-to-default writes the default VALUE (clear reserved for overrides)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same pure model + SaveResult as a1, but reset-to-default writeSetting(segments, catalogDefault) instead of clearSetting.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Identical to a1 except reset-to-default persists the catalog default value; clearSetting is delivered for s4/s5 but unused by s3.
pros: reset-to-default uses the same write path as a normal edit.
cons: Writing the default leaves the key SET (isSet=true), so the row stops reading as default and stops tracking a future default change — not a true reset (ac3).
Rewrites a key the user is un-setting, muddying k4.
Leaves clearSetting unexercised by its owning story, weakening sc2 where it is defined.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Loses on ac3 (write-default is not a true reset) and sc2 (ships clearSetting untested by its owner) — a1 dominates it.

citations.quotedText: 'config.write' handler: params {path: string|string[]; value: unknown} -> setConfigAtPath -> writeFileSync -> reloadChatConfig; returns {ok:true}, or {ok:false} on an invalid path.
setConfigAtPath always ASSIGNS obj[leaf]=value (no delete); toConfigSegments rejects an empty path/segment. A clear is achievable by omitting value so JSON.stringify drops the undefined leaf.
object SettingsView { groupsOf; displayValue } + SettingsGroupModel + interface SettingsSection (declared, unused in S002 — the sc3 seam).
interface DaemonGateway over DaemonRpc.call(method, params): DaemonResult(ok,data,error); sealed three-state results; S002 added settingsCatalog() + METHOD_CONFIG_CATALOG.
sc2: Settings write surface (segment-aware write + clear) behind a sealed SaveResult; writeSetting(pathSegments,value) -> config.write; clearSetting removes a key; owned by s3, consumed by s4/s5.

citations.ref: HLD constraint k5 (docs/epics/expose-all-daemon-config-settings-via-E20260919b5f333f8/HLD.md) / CLAUDE.md project principles
citations.quotedText: Changing which values are stored is the daemon's job; the plugin remains a thin surface that reads the daemon's schema and current values and writes user edits back, owning no settings semantics or defaults of its own.
